# Execution, interaction and responsibility

This developing view explains how an arrangement operates: triggers, inputs, activity, decisions, sequence and concurrency where relevant, outputs, handoffs, exceptions, continuation and stopping conditions. It connects structure to intended effects without claiming that the design has been proven effective.

For each important handoff, identify producer, recipient, what is transferred, when it is usable, what acceptance means, and who handles missing or inadequate input. Distinguish doing work, answering for the result, deciding exceptions and accepting outcomes. One actor can hold multiple roles, but the responsibilities should remain explicit.

Illustration: Dream reviews admitted source material and retains topics; the owner selects a topic; deeper synthesis and writing follow. Office learning becomes available only after a separate handoff. A topic proposal is not a selected topic, an accepted interpretation or a published result.

Execution may be manual, automated or mixed. Tools follow the need, requirements and role boundaries. Paperclip, Codex and a possible Jev assistance step are contextual possibilities in the example, not prerequisites of the standard.

Implementation instructions, runtime setup and detailed verification methods remain outside this discussion's agreed boundary. Descriptions of process implementation and assessment results remain relevant. EOM-05 and EOM-13 in [the ledger](../../../source-locators.md#source-c43947fdcdae322a) track role semantics and the precise execution boundary.
